rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design that races here is the one scored on the unseen track, and no later iteration can correct it. The best evidence is iteration 10 (score 60.27, best so far), which moved sensor y from 0.03 to 0.06 on the iteration 6 controller. Its gain came mainly from oval progress (0.163 against 0.118), oval rms_error (0.0194 against 0.0293) and oval control effort (1.24 against 1.92). The s-bend and slalom progress were unchanged. Every track still shows one line-loss event per trial and max_error of about 0.063 m, so the excursion is not solved. Gains (kp, kd, ki), speed, footprint, spacing and recovery direction all left the excursion essentially unchanged. The Evaluator's approved candidate (R1) is this same design, and its guidance was to keep y = 0.06 and judge it on max_error, line-loss count and progress. I considered extending y to 0.08 as a single further step. The trend is supported on only one step, and the s-bend and slalom gave no gain, so an untested extrapolation on the final, unseen-track race carries more risk than the expected benefit. I therefore submit the iteration 10 design unchanged: base_speed 1.25, kp 1.5, ki 0, kd 0.15, last_direction, sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 with y = 0.06, 16 mm footprints. Expected result: roughly the iteration 10 scores on the development tracks (about 60) and a similar, uncertain outcome on the unseen track. Hypotheses to check: whether forward placement reduces the drift on the unseen track's bends, and whether progress remains above about 0.16. The measurements requested are max_error, line_loss_events and progress per track, plus steering_oscillation and completion to detect jitter or a finish.
